_comment: Hand-added connectors: paths that exist on the ground and are absent from
my campus's sheet. Everything else in paths.json is their printed linework taken
verbatim, which is why this lives in its own file and its own build stage,
with the count and metres printed on every build.
There are two kinds here and they are tested differently.
LOCAL LINKS close a gap between two nearby parts of the network. They are
validated by ablation on the walk between their own endpoints: remove one,
rebuild, and see whether the detour it was added for comes back.
RESCUES bring a whole stranded fragment into the largest component, and the
endpoint test is meaningless for them — pull one and the fragment is pruned,
so an endpoint stops existing and the measurement compares two snaps onto the
same surviving node. They are validated on SHIPPED METRES instead. The three
here carry 571 m, 409 m and 120 m of drawn path respectively: 1,100 m of my campus's
own linework returned to the routable network for 46 m of connector.
READ THIS BEFORE ADDING ONE. An earlier version of this file had 15 links, and
eleven of them ran PARALLEL to a path my campus already draws. That was the wrong
diagnosis: the gap was never a missing path, it was a DRAWN path that failed
to join the graph, and a straight connector alongside it fixed the number
while leaving two splintered lines down one corridor on screen. The junction
stage in build-walk-network.mjs fixes that cause, and seven of those links
were then shown redundant and deleted.
So: before writing a link, check whether the sheet already draws the path and
the extraction is simply failing to connect it. Only if it genuinely draws
nothing does a link belong here. It must be short, visible in aerial imagery,
and `why` must say what is on the ground and what the sheet does instead.
A rescue may be longer, but its gap is still bounded: seven stranded fragments
were refused because reaching them needs 75 to 117 m of invented path, which
is the automatic bridging step this pipeline deliberately does not have.

properties.why: Hutchison Loop bus stop. The sheet draws the zebra crossing over the road and stops at the kerb; on the ground the crossing lands on a concrete pad with a handrail that ramps down to the south footway, which is plainly visible in imagery. Without it the two footways either side of the road only met 65 m west at the car-park entrance, so an 11 m walk across the road routed 523 ft round three sides of a rectangle.

Service yard behind the Child Development Center. The sheet draws driveway either side of the yard and never joins them across it; imagery shows unbroken tarmac, no kerb and no planting. 23 m on foot, 592 m through the graph.
The open plaza between Fine and Applied Arts and the Kaneko Art Gallery. The sheet draws paths round three sides of a paved plaza and none across it.
Between the STEM Innovation Center and the Learning Resource Center. The drawn walkway stops 11 m short of the walkway it visibly continues into.
Road outside the Administration Building. Both footways are drawn; the carriageway between them is never bridged.
The roundabout arm by Printing Services. The sheet draws crossings on the other approaches and leaves this one unjoined.
Paved apron between the Student Center and CTE. The sheet stops a footway either side of it and draws nothing between.
Paved way between the Library and the Student Center, undrawn on the sheet.

RESCUE: the whole perimeter footway around the south car park — 562 m over 8 nodes — was stranded, because the sheet never joins it to campus. It comes within 9.7 m of the network at the head of the accessible bays, and imagery shows hatched crossing markings and unbroken tarmac across that gap. 9.7 m of connector returns 562 m of drawn path to the routable network.

RESCUE: the service loop past the greenhouses and the construction compound — 393 m over 48 nodes — was stranded. Its closest approach to the network is 15.7 m across a paved yard (94% parking/driveway on the sheet, 4% vegetation in imagery). The straight line clips a run of bleachers standing on that yard; you walk round them, and 15.7 m is the right length for the connection either way.

RESCUE: 100 m of footway by the roundabout, stranded 20.6 m from the network. The gap crosses the roundabout apron — paved in imagery, 0% vegetation — though the sheet classifies part of it as base plane rather than a drawn surface, so this is the least certain of the three rescues.

_rejected_note: Gaps the same sweep found and this file deliberately does NOT close, with the
reason each was turned down. Kept so a later audit does not re-propose them:
they will keep showing up as large detours, and they should. Being near is not
the same as being connected. `at` is the midpoint of the rejected connection.

_rejected.why: ends in a planted bed at the edge of the plaza
crosses a kerb with no dropped ramp
crosses a roof — note buildings.json has no footprint here
dark sunken area with steps — level change not resolvable from imagery
bare earth between two paths, no made surface
